title: Windows host: sync/team test cluster fails on a stock setup
observation: 12 tests across 7 files fail on a stock Windows host (PowerShell, Git-for-Windows, core.symlinks=false) while Linux CI is green: two-way sync retry paths, read-side slow-remote timeout/lock release, force-staged shared publication, the real post-commit hook publish, team route contract (60s timeouts), private attach info-attributes rejection, revert-move safety, static-baseline replacement refs, and the production dependency audit. Test-environment classes (mktemp, symlink EPERM, locale, separator literals) were fixed separately the same day — this residue looks like real win32 behavior differences in git transport/hook execution, not test-env noise.
evidence: npm test 2026-08-04 run 1: 936 tests, 109 fail (env classes included)
npm test 2026-08-04 run 2 (after portability fixes e621292): 936 tests, 915 pass, 14 fail, 6 skip
3 of the 14 fixed same day (5608020: locale precondition, readlink separators, git-dematerialized symlink); the remaining cluster is this finding
timeout signatures 60s (team-route-contract), 33s (post-commit hook), ~10s (sync retries) point at git transport/hook exec divergence on win32
